Data and graph terms as this entry states them: artefact (British spelling) is the system under test, the graph build, while artifact (HERB's spelling) is one source record in the corpus carrying an id - the citation id space - and the two are never mixed. A Chunk is ONE graph retrieval unit or source locator whose locator_json selects records in a raw file; a chunk is never 'a record' or 'hundreds of records', and resolved artifact ids are the citation-space records its locator covers. Hard fields are chunk attributes (product, section, channel, employee_id, years, relevance_to_file); Tag/HAS_TAG edges carry w_chunk plus aligned facets and w_facets plus run_id; Facets are topic / entities / activity / temporal / evidence. contexts are the resolved chunk texts handed to the generator, k of them being the shared top-k evidence budget, while context_ids are artifact ids off the resolved records deduped in rank order and NOT aligned 1:1 with contexts - so truncate_k slicing context_ids[:k] is invalid for the artefact arm. gold citations are a question's citations; the corpus is oracle-stripped with truth read from raw by evaluators only; gold-100 and 10smoke are fixed question-id sets, and question ids are <product>::a|u::<index>
